title: Reserve allocator warmup deadlock causing reserved-pool starvation during rapid rollback
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Summary:
During a rapid rollback of a scale-controller change in eu-west-1 (automatic rollback triggered by a faulty canary), the reserve allocator entered a warmup deadlock that prevented reserved-pool headroom from being replenished. Impact: multiple Dedicated customers experienced sustained 'cold' capacity for up to 17 minutes; burst requests were dropped or shed despite apparent free GPU capacity in underlying hosts.

Observed behavior and scope:
- Symptom: allocator showed high 'warmup_pending' tokens for affected tenants while reserved-pool free slots remained non-zero on hosts (inconsistent accounting).
- Affected surface: reserved pools in eu-west-1, small-to-medium tenants relying on burst credits; roughly 4 customer tenants reported degraded throughput and increased 503 error rates.
- Trigger: rapid rollback sequence + leader re-election where warmup leases were not reclaimed and candidate reclaims raced with the rollback path, leaving warmup entries in an un-reclaimable state.

Root cause hypothesis (confirmed by logs):
- Warmup lease lifecycle assumed monotonic controller ownership; under rapid leader churn (rollback -> restart -> leader-election), some warmup leases were persisted with an opaque owner id and no expiry checkpoint. The rollback path removed some allocator indexes while leaving warmup ledger entries referencing the old allocator shard. The reconciliation loop relies on heartbeats to expire leases, but heartbeats were suppressed during the rollback window causing a multi-minute stuck state.

Immediate mitigations applied (hotfix timeline):
- 2026-03-05 09:02 UTC: Enabled emergency fallback route policy to temporarily direct new burst requests to a pooled-host fallback path (hosted ephemeral pool) for affected tenants. Deployed via config toggle (feature.flag.fallback_pool=true).
- 2026-03-05 09:12 UTC: Deployed hotpatch (PR #github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3128) that adds an allocator-level warmup-lease TTL (default 30s) and a background reaper that will forcibly reclaim warmup tokens older than TTL. Hotpatch rolled to 25% canary->50%->100% over 30 minutes.
- 2026-03-05 09:20 UTC: Manual reconciliation run: runbook execute 'allocator reconcile --region eu-west-1 --scan-warmup --force-reclaim' to flush stuck entries for impacted pools.
- 2026-03-05 09:30 UTC: Observed steady recovery; customer 1 restored to normal burst behavior by 09:38 UTC, others recovered in the following 15 minutes.

Permanent fixes proposed and design decisions:
1) Stronger lease invariants and re-entrancy: always attach a wall-clock expiry to warmup leases and encode leader epoch into the lease so a new leader can safely detect stale ownership. (Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DAR/Allocator+Warmup+Lease+Spec)
2) Rollback-safe allocator upgrades: ensure allocator index and ledger updates are performed in a transactional two-phase pattern with a rollback compensating action that reclaims any in-flight warmup entries referencing removed indexes.
3) Observability: add Grafana panels and alerting for warmup_pending_ratio > 0.05 sustained for 2m, and warmup_lease_age_p95 > 10s. Dashboards created: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/allocator/allocator-warmup (panel ids included in attachments).
4) Safety net: implement a cross-pool fallback router that transparently routes requests to a globally shared ephemeral pool when reserved-pool headroom is inconsistent for >45s. This keeps SLA for P1/P0 customers while allocator reconciliation occurs.

Acceptance criteria for release-1.22 fix:
- No warmup token age > 60s in canary under injected rapid leader churn (chaos test).
- End-to-end telemetry demonstrates reclaimed stuck warmup tokens within TTL in >99% cases.
- Canary rollouts show no increase in 503s for reserved-pool tenants under synthetic burst load.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- TTL selection: shorter TTL reduces impact window but increases churn from transient scheduler pauses; chosen default 30s with canary adjustments.
- Cost vs reliability of fallback pool: fallback pool consumes additional reserved infra when used; will be configurable per customer tier.

Risk & rollback plan:
- Risk: aggressive TTL might cause premature reclaim during long legitimate warmups (very large model cold-starts). Mitigation: per-tenant override and health probe to detect long-running legitimate warmups.
- Rollback: the hotpatch is feature-flagged; canary rollback is immediate by disabling feature.flag.warmup_ttl or rolling back PR in runtime branch.

Links / artifacts:
- Hotpatch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3128
- Runbook used: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DAR/Reserved+Pool+Reconcile+Runbook
- Grafana panels: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/allocator/allocator-warmup
- Slack incident thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01ALLOCATE/p1678012345678900
